dialog.survivorcolonies.recruit.confirm_: I would gladly join your colony! As provisions, I'll need %sx %s. Do we have a deal?
dialog.survivorcolonies.recruit.main: Hello traveler! It's good to see a friendly face. How can I help you?
dialog.survivorcolonies.recruit.skills_i: I have the following skills to offer:
dialog.survivorcolonies.recruit.story_1: I hid in an old cave for days... The hordes out there are getting more aggressive by the day.
dialog.survivorcolonies.recruit.story_2: My old camp was ambushed. I'm the only one who made it here.
dialog.survivorcolonies.recruit.story_3: I wandered through the wilderness for weeks, always searching for a safe settlement.
dialog.survivorcolonies.trade.done: A good trade. Take care out there.
dialog.survivorcolonies.trade.empty: I currently have absolutely nothing in my backpack that I could spare.
dialog.survivorcolonies.trade.haggle_acc: %sx %s? Yes, that's a fair trade. Let's do business.
dialog.survivorcolonies.trade.haggle_rej: Only %sx %s? That's not enough. I need more of that.
dialog.survivorcolonies.trade.has_items: This is what I've gathered on my travels. What do you need?
dialog.survivorcolonies.trade.player_emp: You don't have anything on you that would be worth a fair trade.
dialog.survivorcolonies.trade.player_off: So you want my %s? Okay, what will you give me in return?

gui.survivorcolonies.recruit.title: Survivor

gui.survivorcolonies.dialog.title: Talk
survivorcolonies.dialog.resume.high_trus: Good to have you back, %s! We were just talking:
Ah, my favorite person in this camp. Where were we? Ah yes:
There you are! I was still thinking about what we said earlier:
survivorcolonies.dialog.resume.low_trust: Back again? Let's just finish what we started:
You again... make it quick. We were at:
survivorcolonies.dialog.resume.grumpy.0: What do you want now? Right, we were talking about this:
survivorcolonies.dialog.resume.grumpy.1: I'm busy, %s. But fine, where were we? Ah:
Gah! Don't sneak up on me! Right... before you startled me, we were on:
Oh, thank goodness it's just you. Quick, back to what we were saying:
Took you long enough to return, %s. As I was saying earlier:
Hey there, %s! Great to see you again! As we were saying:
Welcome back by the fire! We were right in the middle of this:
survivorcolonies.dialog.resume.cynical.0: Still alive? Good. Let's wrap up that thought before our luck runs out:
survivorcolonies.dialog.resume.mysteriou: The winds brought you back, %s. Our thread was left hanging right here:
survivorcolonies.dialog.resume.default.0: Ah, you again. As we were saying:
survivor.npc.1: Keep your hands where I can see them, stranger. Not many friendly faces out in these woods.
survivor.npc.2: You tread loudly for someone wandering the rot-woods. Who are you and what do you want?
survivor.npc.3: Stay back. I don't know you, and out here, that means I don't trust you.
survivor.npc.4: Didn't think I'd run into another living soul out here. Are you alone?
survivor.npc.5: The fog is rolling in thick. If you don't have shelter, you're not going to last the night out here.
survivor.npc.6: Look at the sky... a storm is brewing. You'd better keep moving if you know what's good for you.
survivor.npc.7: These woods change when the sun goes down. I hope for your sake you aren't planning to camp in the open.
survivor.npc.8: Can you hear that? The silence in these trees always precedes a hunt.
survivor.npc.9: If you're looking to rob me of my rations, you'll find nothing but disappointment and a fight.
survivor.npc.10: I haven't eaten a hot meal in a week. Don't suppose you have any spare jerky in that pack of yours?
survivor.npc.11: Foraging out here is a fool's errand. Everything is either poisonous or already picked clean.
survivor.npc.12: I found this snare empty again. The game out here is getting scarce... or something bigger is eating it.
survivor.npc.13: I wouldn't step off the path if I were you. I saw tracks the size of a wagon tire just over the ridge.
survivor.npc.14: Did your camp send you out here to die? Wandering this deep into the wild is a death sentence.
survivor.npc.15: I've been surviving out here on my own for months. I don't need dead weight slowing me down.
survivor.npc.16: Keep your voice down! Do you want to draw the %4$s right to us?
survivor.npc.17: I've been walking since my settlement burned to the ground. Don't suppose you come from a safe haven, do you?
survivor.npc.18: I used to travel with a caravan. Now it's just me. The less you know about what happened to them, the better.
survivor.npc.19: People say there's an intact colony beyond the river gorge. I'm starting to think it's just a fairy tale.
survivor.npc.20: You look as exhausted as I feel. If we don't kill each other, maybe we can share a fire tonight.
survivor.npc.21: I was tracking some scavengers through this hollow, but I lost their trail at the creek.
survivor.npc.22: My blade is dull and I'm out of clean bandages. Running into you is either a blessing or my final curse.
survivor.npc.23: I once was an adventurer like you...
survivor.npc.24: Stay a while and listen, stranger! The forest feels far too quiet tonight.
survivor.npc.25: Wandering this wasteland almost makes you wish for a nuclear winter.
survivor.npc.26: Praise the sun! I didn't think I'd survive another night in the open.
survivor.npc.27: Someone carved a sign saying there was a supply drop out here, but I'm pretty sure the cake is a lie.
survivor.npc.28: It's dangerous to go alone in these woods. Not that I'm offering to join you.
survivor.npc.29: War never changes, and neither does the stench of this swamp.
survivor.npc.30: did that scarecrow we propped up by the pumpkin patch just turn its head?
survivor.npc.31: If anyone asks, I didn't challenge the traveling blacksmith to an arm-wrestling match. And my shoulder is totally fine.If you're a hallucination from eating those blue mushrooms, you're the most boring one yet.
survivor.npc.32: I've been talking to a stump for three days. You're an upgrade, I guess.
survivor.npc.33: Godslayer, good day! Er, wait, you're just some guy with a backpack.
survivor.npc.34: A raccoon made off with my left boot last night. Don't look at my feet.
survivor.npc.35: I didn't steal those shiny rocks from the crow's nest, and if anyone asks, neither did you.
survivor.npc.36: Are you the guy who's been leaving weird stick figures tied to the trees, or is that just local decor?
survivor.npc.37: If anyone asks, I absolutely did not run screaming from a badger about an hour ago.
survivor.npc.38: Good. I appreciate a clear mind like yours; it's rare these days. Tell me, what was your family doing back near %3$s?
survivor.npc.39: Hmph. Fine. You talk a good game about intent, but nothing convinces me after the last thing I saw near %3$s. Tell me, what sort of grueling work keeps you going out here? Because physical grit is the only currency that matters.
survivor.npc.40: Say that and I'll believe you. Most people only talk the talk until the next threat comes sniffing around. Tell me, what kind of stories do you have from %3$s? Maybe there was something about them worth hearing.
survivor.npc.41: Alright, alright. Just... watch yourself. You've got a bit of fire in you, haven't you? Tell me about the time things really went sideways back near your old home.
survivor.npc.42: Well, you certainly have spirit! Maybe I'm too cautious, or maybe... perhaps you just remind me of a life before all this dust. Tell me, what was your favorite place to wander?
survivor.npc.43: I know you're capable, %1$s, and I don't want to sound paranoid, but let’s just walk together for now. Tell me about your journey; maybe you can tell me what life was like before the fall of %3$s.
survivor.npc.44: Alright, alright. Just... try not to make a scene, okay? You know, it reminds me of the time I used to live near %3$s. Things were much quieter back then.
survivor.npc.45: Alright, alright. I'm not going anywhere. You know, when things were different back in %3$s, we used to... (pauses, a wistful look) ...tell stories almost every night.
survivor.npc.46: Look, I just... you make me nervous. It's been so long since we had a proper meal; my stomach makes noises all the time. Tell me, what was your family like back near %3$s? Were they good at growing food?
survivor.npc.47: A higher purpose, eh? I've heard enough talk like this in my life, %1$s. Tell me something real; what brought you all the way out here from where you were?
survivor.npc.48: Higher purpose? All I see is wasted time and noise. You talk of rising up, but can you even afford a decent meal? Tell me about %3$s's harvests—what truly sustains it?
survivor.npc.49: Knowledge... yes. It is a strange wind that blows through the ruins these days. But every truth, even one promising rebirth for %3$s, carries echoes of forgotten pain.
survivor.npc.50: Easy now, kid. Nobody likes a fight over who gets to walk past them. What was it you were doing out in these woods that made you so reckless?
survivor.npc.51: Careful. Such insolence doesn't suit a wanderer who hasn't seen the horrors of %3$s. If you waste my time, I might just ask questions that are harder to answer than your name.
survivor.npc.52: Oh dear. You've got bite to you! But hey, since we're wasting time anyway, tell me, what treasures have you stumbled upon near your homeland? Maybe we can trade stories for some coin.
survivor.npc.53: Easy now, there's no need for dramatic pronouncements in this place. Tell me, what was it you lost back at %3$s that made you think the rot-woods were an appropriate grave for your melodrama?
survivor.npc.54: Easy now. Don't let the gloom get to you; you know I wouldn't judge a friend, no matter what shadows trail behind them.
survivor.npc.55: Oh, don't talk like that! You really are the most dramatic person I know. But hey, since you're here now, let's skip the brooding and hear about your family history instead—I bet it's a wilder tale than all this gloomy weather!
survivor.npc.56: Nervous, are you? Look, I'm not sure what 'helping' means out here, but maybe we can talk about it later. If you want to know anything, ask me about %3$s instead.
survivor.npc.57: Help? You think 'help' is a promise I can taste like rain and sunshine? Everything good out here was just another story that failed, %1$s. It always ends the same way.
survivor.npc.58: Help, you say? I... I saw how you handled that busted comms array earlier. Your touch was remarkably steady. Maybe we can talk about what happened before all this started.
survivor.npc.59: A community center? Seriously? This isn't some overgrown theme park, kid. Look, if you want to talk about 'normal,' we need to talk about what happened at %3$s.
survivor.npc.60: You talk about community centers? Out here, things are far more complicated than simple structures. I believe understanding the past is how we find a way forward.
survivor.npc.61: You don't care about me, do you? You just ask about a community center. Seems like nobody remembers how to be scared out here.
survivor.npc.62: You really are a peculiar one, aren't you? Look, if you want stories, I have plenty—stories about life before all this and what happened in %3$s.
survivor.npc.63: Nap spot? Don't be ridiculous. You think my time is for some weary scavenger's rest stop? If you want tips on how to survive, at least show me a little respect.
survivor.npc.64: A nap spot? Ha. Nothing's free out here, especially not a comfortable one. But... if you want to talk about valuables and survival, I might know a spot that paid for its rest.
survivor.npc.65: Look, I don't know what kind of jokes you're running, but we're all too tired for that. Just tell me—what happened to your side of the settlement?
survivor.npc.66: Ha! You have quite the sense of humor. Speaking of wandering... you know, when I was building my filtration rig back in %3$s, I once used a discarded autolytica panel to create an emergency radio antenna. It was certainly unorthodox!
survivor.npc.67: A little sarcasm won't build a roof over your head. If you're so keen on 'zones,' perhaps you could tell me what kind of useful goods you might trade, and we can talk.
survivor.npc.68: Right, 'operational status.' Look, I don't care about your fancy talk; it just sounds exhausting. You know, speaking of managing things... you wouldn't believe what we lost when the Raiders hit %3$s.
survivor.npc.69: Resource allocation? My dear, we're not discussing quarterly reports; we're talking survival. But tell me, what sort of goods do you trade with this 'operational status'? Perhaps there's something I can barter for information.
survivor.npc.70: Resource allocation? You talk like you manage quarterly reports. I’ve dealt with things that chew through steel and don't care about your 'operational status.' Tell me, what happened to your people back in %3$s?
survivor.npc.71: Solo, huh? Alright. Well, since we're standing here talking instead of running from trouble, maybe you can tell me what life was like before... well, before everything went to hell in %3$s.
survivor.npc.72: Trade? Of course. Just... don't make any sudden moves. My name is %2$s, and I know a few things about survival that might interest you, if you listen first.
survivor.npc.73: Trade? Everything's got a price out here. My stuff isn't for charity, but maybe you know something I don't... about the old settlement, %3$s?
survivor.npc.74: A higher truth? Look, I don't know about your 'curtains,' but we need practical solutions right now. You reminded me of something... when my family was trapped in %3$s, we had to figure out shelter with almost nothing.
survivor.npc.75: A 'higher truth,' you say? Save your sermons. I know what survival looks like—sweat, muscle, and hauling lumber until your back screams. We're doing this the hard way.
survivor.npc.76: A higher truth? You speak like someone who has never lost anything dear. Don't you remember the way life used to be?
survivor.npc.77: It's not concern, it's just survival sense. Frankly, everyone here needs shelter when the fog rolls in; we lost so much back at %3$s that I know what happens to unprepared people.
survivor.npc.78: Suspicion is a luxury we can't afford right now. You think I care about your shelter? I just remember what it was like to lose everything—to see our whole %3$s swallowed by the mist.
survivor.npc.79: Trick you? You think I care about your lodging, %1$s? After years of scraping by on broken promises and nothing but grit, a little concern isn't going to break me. Just keep moving.
survivor.npc.80: It's not about where we get our materials right now; survival is the only priority. Speaking of tough times, do you remember what happened to your family back near %3$s? I bet you have some stories.
survivor.npc.81: Some things are woven from necessity, little sprout. The materials used to keep us alive often tell stories that the living prefer to forget.
survivor.npc.82: Materials are secondary right now. We need sturdy walls against the night; I’m far more worried about what comes out of that fog than any stray meal.
survivor.npc.83: You don't have to convince me of anything, %1$s. We were just talking about the storm, but speaking of difficult times... it reminds me of what happened back in %3$s when we lost everything.
survivor.npc.84: Shelter together? Don't be foolish. You think I care about your company when the very ground beneath us could swallow me whole? Just... keep your distance.
survivor.npc.85: You certainly have an adventurous spirit. Speaking of difficult times and needing shelter... %2$s remembers a time when the storm almost took everything from our little community in %3$s.
survivor.npc.86: Destiny? Now, %1$s, let’s not get carried away with grand pronouncements. I'm more concerned with finding a dry place to sleep tonight. Speaking of darkness, do you remember what happened to your family when the raiders hit %3$s? It was a mess.
survivor.npc.87: Destiny? Don't speak of grand destinies when you can barely look at the ground. You talk too much about what is to come, %1$s, and nothing but trouble ever follows that kind of arrogance.
survivor.npc.88: You speak of destiny, %1$s, but I remember only the taste of blood and ripped flesh. We survived because we were lucky—or perhaps simply desperate.
survivor.npc.89: It's just survival, kid. We move when we have to, or the scavengers find us first. Honestly, you always were too concerned with yourself.
survivor.npc.90: You always ask the most impractical questions. Honestly, I'm more concerned with how the structural integrity of these old bridges will hold up before we get to any talk of pacing.
survivor.npc.91: Lag behind? This isn't a stroll through the market; this is survival. If you lack the stamina to keep pace, perhaps you should consider if staying here isn't a more tactically sound choice.
survivor.npc.92: You have a way of speaking that makes me think you haven't seen much of the world. Was life before this mess really so different, or was it always just hanging over us?
survivor.npc.93: Nonsense. You obsess over feelings when you should be thinking about locks and perimeter warnings. Nothing changes but the danger we face, something I've seen a thousand times in %3$s.
survivor.npc.94: You speak in riddles, %1$s. It's a convenient way to distract from the things you don't want to face. Let me tell you about what really happened at %3$s; it was far stranger than any forest can be.
survivor.npc.95: You have a bizarre sense of humor, %1$s, but I'm not arguing with you about meteorology or snacks right now. We should talk about what happened to your family before the outbreak.
survivor.npc.96: Don't you dare talk about 'snacks' like that. You have no idea what life is like out here, %1$s. We lost so much near %3$s before this... I wish people would just take things seriously.
survivor.npc.97: Snacks? You think this is about snacks. My concern has nothing to do with your silly jokes; it's survival. Speaking of things that matter, have you ever heard the stories of what we lost down in %3$s? It was a struggle for every single scrap.
survivor.npc.98: Right, right. Just... be careful out there. You know, when things got bad at %3$s, we used to survive mostly by staying close to the old stone walls, before the woods even knew what a monster was.
survivor.npc.99: Such certainty. It reminds me of the oaths sworn on the road—oaths that meant everything to us at the time, when our life depended on every wagon wheel turning.
survivor.npc.100: Hmph. 'No threat shall penetrate.' Such bold words for someone who hasn't seen the real darkness we dealt with near %3$s. You speak of watch, but you know nothing of true vigilance.
survivor.npc.101: Now, now, let's keep the melodrama for later. We need a plan that won't draw attention. Speaking of beasts... do you know anything about what happened to your family near %3$s? I heard some wild tales.
survivor.npc.102: Whoa, easy there. You speak with such confidence! It reminds me of tales back in %3$s, when we used to face down things much worse than just a hunt.
survivor.npc.103: Find the beast, you say? Always so sure of yourself. You forget that even in a scout group, paranoia can be as deadly as any %4$s. Tell me about your last patrol, what you saw that made you sound so confident.
survivor.npc.104: You're right, I apologize. It's just that the quiet makes me jumpy; it reminds me of what happened near %3$s. Do you remember when we first got here?
survivor.npc.105: Working in tandem? You always think you're the reliable pillar, %1$s. But reliability is a myth. Tell me about your time at %3$s; what did they teach you about true partnership?
survivor.npc.106: You are right. The plan… it always begins with understanding the shadows of where we came from. Do you remember what happened at %3$s? I fear that much echoes here.
survivor.npc.107: You'd better focus, %1$s. We don't have time for distractions or childish games; we need to talk about what happened at %3$s.
survivor.npc.108: You... you just giggle about berries? You sound like a lost thing. Leave the woods alone; you're drawing attention to us, and we don't need any more trouble.
survivor.npc.109: You distract yourself with trinkets and berries; it’s hardly a challenge. But since you persist in being... enthusiastic, let me tell you about the time I navigated the Whisperwoods before the blight hit %3$s. It's quite different from your little skirmishes.
survivor.npc.110: Look, just stop with the weird jokes and get serious. You don't know anything about what we went through at %3$s.
survivor.npc.111: Keep your gibberish to yourself. If you're going to waste my time with that juvenile nonsense, we're finished right here.
survivor.npc.112: Don't play around with me. You think mockery is a shield? We need to talk about what you really want, because I know nothing is free in this world—especially not information.
survivor.npc.113: Look, I don't know what your game is, but threatening people isn't going to help you survive here. You should talk to me, and maybe we can talk about what happened at %3$s before all this.
survivor.npc.114: You think brute force solves everything? You're just like the rest of them—greedy fools who never understood that a simple lockpick and a good alibi are worth more than any fight.
survivor.npc.115: Aggressive posturing rarely pays well. Let's dispense with the theatrics; if there's value in a conversation, it exists only through calculated risk and mutual benefit.
survivor.npc.116: Look, I don't know what kind of gag you're having, but let's just talk about something else. Do you even know anything about the Old Quarter? Because that reminds me of when we used to live in %3$s...
survivor.npc.117: Haha! You always have a way of making things sound ridiculous. But hey, enough about petty arguments; did you know that when I was growing up in %3$s, we used to make the best bread? It needed three special ingredients!
survivor.npc.118: Shoes? You think I spend my time on frivolous nonsense when there are real trade routes to be secured? Honestly, you'd find a more honest exchange of stories with someone who remembers the good times back in %3$s.
survivor.npc.119: A nutrient paste? You and your 'elements from various eras' sound like a lot of trouble. Just tell me about what life was like back in %3$s, before all this.
survivor.npc.120: Hmph. Synthesizing? Of course you can. I suppose your 'complex' rations are far beyond the need for simple jerky, but tell me, what was life like when your time machine wasn't broken down in this ruin?
survivor.npc.121: Synthesize? You think I'm some kind of lab experiment for your weird 'temporal rations'? Don't confuse my caution with generosity, %1$s; you haven't earned a single crumb of trust from %2$s.
survivor.npc.122: Venison, huh? You really do have supplies. Speaking of things we once had... it reminds me of the harvest at %3$s before everything went wrong.
survivor.npc.123: Don't patronize me with pity, %1$s. You always think you can just hand out scraps like we’re still living in some kind of gilded cage. It’s never about the jerky, is it? It's about nothing else.
survivor.npc.124: It's good to know someone around here has some foresight. Speaking of supplies, what did you remember about the perimeter patrol routes before everything went sideways at %3$s? I always wondered how many checkpoints we even had.
survivor.npc.125: Right, I get it. Look, if you're not going to talk about anything else, maybe you can tell me about your time before the collapse? What was life like in %3$s?
survivor.npc.126: You sound like you haven't had a decent meal yourself. Don't lecture me on scarcity when your own supplies look almost bare, %1$s. It just reminds me of what happened to us at %3$s.
survivor.npc.127: Now, now. There are always costs, even for a simple snack. But since you seem to require... *guidance* on basic etiquette, tell me instead about your time in %3$s. Was there much trade passing through?
survivor.npc.128: Well, %1$s, I don't know what kind of dramatic performance you think this is, but please just stick to the plan. Do you remember when my family had to leave %3$s? We learned that showboating rarely bought us supper.
survivor.npc.129: Such bravado. You speak of proving things with a confidence that borders on the theatrical; perhaps you should spend less time on grand posturing and more time studying local flora, like I used to do back in %3$s.
survivor.npc.130: Such grand pronouncements. While your confidence is... notable, relying on flair rather than actual strategy is merely a variable I haven't factored in yet. Tell me, %1$s, where exactly did you learn such theatrical displays of competence?
survivor.npc.131: Don't be ridiculous, %1$s. Focus on what you need to say. Frankly, I haven't time for games; we should talk about how this whole settlement collapsed and why.
survivor.npc.132: Don't try that. My focus is on survival, not foolish games. You always were too dramatic for your own good.
survivor.npc.133: Such frivolous concerns. I have seen histories—and flora—far more intricate than merely 'pretty.' Perhaps you would be interested in the forgotten medicinal properties of Ironbark sap, a knowledge far beyond typical foraging.
survivor.npc.134: I don't know, %1$s. I just worry about the risk. You sound overly confident... it reminds me of what happened to my family near %3$s.
survivor.npc.135: A shared outing? You sound dangerously cheerful, %1$s. If you insist on wasting time with such optimistic nonsense, at least let me share something useful. Do you know anything about the old research station near %3$s?
survivor.npc.136: Ah, 'mamma mia,' you say? Well, if we're going to salvage this trip, we need more than just good spots; we need *trade*. I once sourced a whole caravan of edible moss from the Black Peaks—a far cry from any mere foraging. Tell me, what have your little 'spots' got that I can barter with?
survivor.npc.137: Hold up, man. Let's keep the big talk for when we actually got something solid. But you've got a point; things have been bad since... well, back when it happened to %3$s.
survivor.npc.138: Easy, now. Don't get jumpy. We need to keep our hands steady and our perimeter intact. Remember what happened at %3$s when the last scavenge run failed?
survivor.npc.139: Whoa, easy there. You got a point about the woods, but you gotta understand how deep this hole goes... I remember when we had a spot like %3$s, and resources were never an issue.
survivor.npc.140: You always think of a practical fix, don't you? It reminds me of something my family used to do back in %3$s; we had to be creative with what little was left.
survivor.npc.141: Adjusting traps... yes. You focus on the mechanism, I suppose. It reminds me of how we used to set snares near %3$s, back before everything broke down.
survivor.npc.142: It's always something, isn't it? You know, when I ran away from the Vanguard—the sheer number of eyes on me… it taught me to be too careful for easy fixes. We need to think bigger than just traps.
survivor.npc.143: Hold on, let's not jump to conclusions about people. You know, when things got truly bad at %3$s, we had to ration everything just to make it through the winter.
survivor.npc.144: Perimeter? You think the problems are *out* here? The rot started closer to home. Let's talk about what you haven't noticed, %1$s.
survivor.npc.145: Hoarding? No... no one would dare. You remind me of the elders at %3$s—they always worried about what others took, but we survived on pure grit and knowing where to find a clean meal.
survivor.npc.146: Easy now, %1$s. You sound like you've forgotten we're still survivors; the path is only safe because of its history. Let me tell you about what was once built here at %3$s...
survivor.npc.147: A good question, %1$s. It seems we've both got a sense of adventure. Let me tell you about the time I was scouting near my old home in %3$s—I saw things far stranger than tire tracks.
survivor.npc.148: You have no idea what you're talking about. You think this is a gamble? Nothing leads to dinner for us, only the memory of what we lost.
survivor.npc.149: Slow down, %1$s. We need safe bets right now, not grand plans for the ridge line. Tell me more about what you saw back in %3$s that made people think that was smart.
survivor.npc.150: Flanking it... you speak with the confidence of someone who hasn't seen true danger. When I was stationed at %3$s, we only moved when our purpose and duty demanded it.
